name: Battle of Shanghai
summary: The first major battle of the Second Sino-Japanese War, fought over three brutal months in China's most modern city after Chiang Kai-shek committed his best-trained divisions to defend it. Japanese forces finally broke through in November 1937, and the surviving Chinese army withdrew toward Nanjing.

name: Fall of Nanjing & Nanjing Massacre
summary: After Shanghai fell, Japanese forces took China's capital within days in December 1937. What followed defined the event: roughly six weeks of mass executions and widespread sexual violence, one of the worst atrocities of the twentieth century.

name: Invasion of Poland
summary: Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939 using Blitzkrieg tactics, fast tank and air formations that shattered Polish defences within weeks, while a Soviet invasion from the east on 17 September sealed the country's fate. Britain and France's declarations of war in response marked the formal start of the Second World War in Europe.

name: Battle of France
summary: Germany launched Case Yellow on 10 May 1940, rapidly overwhelming Allied forces through Blitzkrieg tactics and a surprise advance through the Ardennes. The campaign resulted in the fall of France, the evacuation at Dunkirk, and left Britain standing alone against Nazi Germany.

name: Evacuation of Dunkirk (Operation Dynamo)
summary: As Allied forces became trapped on the beaches of Dunkirk, Britain launched Operation Dynamo to evacuate them across the English Channel. Over 338,000 British and French troops escaped, preserving Britain's army despite abandoning most of its equipment.

name: Battle of Britain
summary: Following the fall of France, Germany sought to destroy the Royal Air Force before launching Operation Sea Lion, the planned invasion of Britain. Despite being heavily outnumbered, the RAF successfully defended British skies, forcing Hitler to postpone the invasion indefinitely and marking Germany's first major defeat of the war.

name: Operation Barbarossa
summary: On 22 June 1941, Germany launched the largest military operation in history, sending three million soldiers across a 2,900km front into the Soviet Union in a war Hitler conceived from the outset as one of racial annihilation rather than conventional conquest. Stalin had refused to believe the invasion was coming, and Soviet defences were almost entirely unprepared when it arrived.

name: Attack on Pearl Harbor
summary: On 7 December 1941, Japan launched a surprise carrier-based air strike on the US Pacific Fleet at Pearl Harbor, killing 2,404 people and destroying or damaging 21 ships and 347 aircraft. Japan hoped the attack would cripple America into suing for peace, but it instead brought the United States fully into the war on both fronts.

name: Invasion of Malaya
summary: Japanese forces landed at Kota Bharu on the northeast coast of British Malaya within hours of the Pearl Harbor attack, using bicycles and coastal landings to repeatedly outflank Commonwealth defenders despite being outnumbered. By 31 January 1942 the last British troops had withdrawn across the causeway into Singapore, which engineers then demolished behind them.

name: Fall of Singapore
summary: Although Commonwealth troops outnumbered the attacking Japanese roughly two to one, General Percival misjudged the main axis of attack and the garrison collapsed within a week of the assault beginning on 8 February 1942. Percival surrendered on 15 February in what Churchill called the worst disaster in British military history.

name: Siege of Leningrad
summary: Encircled by German forces from September 1941, Leningrad was subjected to sustained shelling and deliberate starvation, with civilian rations falling to as little as 125 grams of bread a day. A precarious supply route across frozen Lake Ladoga sustained the city until a Soviet offensive broke the siege on 27 January 1944, killing roughly 800,000 civilians.
